label: lad-be3c9
summary: The network adds eight ReLU units over the board, and they read as board-evaluation features about the lower centre: x pieces on the centre column d and on the second and third rows of columns c-e raise x's predicted win chance, and o pieces there lower it. The largest part, unit 1, rewards x pieces stacked on top of o in the centre (switching it off lowers the training AUC from 0.902 to 0.782); unit 4 (o on the bottom-row centre squares c1 and d1) and unit 8 (o on c2 or c3) lower the prediction, and unit 7 damps the reward for x on d3. On the data the mean predicted win chance is 84% where x has more pieces than o in column d and 43% where o has more.

resisted: Unit 7 has no reading beyond a brake on the reward for x on d3; its activity in the 24318 positions without x on d3 is unexplained. Unit 8's rise with x on e3 and f3 has no reading. Unit 2's strongest regime (x on b1, c1 and d1, 43 positions, o blocking both ends) predicts 77% on average where x wins 28%: the model's reading of that line does not match the game. Each unit has a weight on each square; the readings name the heaviest squares on the data and leave the rest to the closed forms.

recheck_notes: No mismatch and no needs_review item. An earlier run flagged the unit_activity query as computed before the last structural operation; it was recomputed after the structure was final (q_1a02e8dae0) and every reference moved to it. The unchecked free-text sentences are qualitative readings of which squares raise or lower each unit, backed by the attached closed forms and the self-probes rather than by a single number.
tool_bugs: None blocking. xn.py --recheck --record fails with FileNotFoundError if the record file does not exist yet. A composition cannot group leaves without nodes of its own (the hidden units are covered by the leaves), so the hierarchy is eight leaves under one root. get_formula returns no provenance id, so formula evidence is a payload and its tolerance is quoted from check_explanation.

refuted_and_fixed: xBottomLeftRow: the bottom-row line reading implies x usually wins with x on b1, c1 and d1, but in those training positions o blocks both ends and x wins far less often than the model predicts; the hypothesis now says the regime is fitted and does not match the game

oBottomCentre: a draft implied o on c1 and d1 lowers the whole-model prediction; the probe shows it does not on the empty board because unit 1 rises more, and the hypothesis now says so with the part contributions

leaves.name: xCentreAboveOBottom
leaves.why: Rewards x pieces on the second and third rows of the centre sitting on top of o's bottom-row centre pieces; the d-column probe and the stacked-column subgroups confirm it.

leaves.name: xBottomLeftRow
leaves.why: Detects x building a line along a1-d1 of the bottom row (the probe confirms it), but its strongest regime is fitted to a few dozen positions where o has blocked both ends and x wins far less often than predicted.

leaves.name: xCentreThirdRow
leaves.why: Opens for x on the third-row centre squares d3 and c3; the probe and the d3 subgroups confirm it.

leaves.name: oBottomCentre
leaves.why: Grows with o on the bottom-row centre squares c1 and d1 and lowers the win chance; the probe and the subgroup where o holds both confirm it.

leaves.name: xOnC2
leaves.why: Opens mainly for x on c2 (helped by c3 and d3); the probe and the c2 subgroups confirm it.

leaves.name: xLowColumnD
leaves.why: Rewards x owning the low squares of the centre column (d2, d1, d3); the d1-by-d2 probe and the d2 subgroups confirm it.

leaves.name: xHighColumnD
leaves.why: Reads as a brake on the reward the other units give for x on d3 (the probe confirms it), but its activity in many positions without x on d3 has no reading.

leaves.name: xRightOCentre
leaves.why: Grows with o on c2 or c3 (probe and subgroups confirm it), but its rise with x on e3 and f3 has no reading.

overall_function: The network scores how well x controls the lower centre of the board: x pieces on the centre column and on the second and third rows of columns c to e raise the predicted win chance, and o pieces there lower it. The bottom row is treated differently: one unit rewards x pieces stacked on top of o's bottom-row centre pieces while another penalises o holding c1 and d1, so the two partly cancel, and a separate gate adds a bonus when x builds a line along the left of the bottom row. The units are added and passed through a sigmoid with no direct square-to-output edges, and one unit acts as a brake on the large combined reward for x on d3. Squares away from the lower centre carry smaller weights in the readings, but none is ignored outright.
stuck: Coverage and operations were straightforward (42 input splits, eight single-unit leaves, one root). Leaf meaning was the hard part: each unit weighs every square, so readings name the heaviest squares on the data, and units 2, 7 and 8 keep behaviour without a domain reading. Constructed probes use an otherwise empty board, which is not a legal 8-ply position; data subgroups were added to check the readings on real positions.
